dedupe_keys.name: key results from applied element method collapse simulations of rc buildings with selected features preliminary

description: This small dataset gives key results from progressive collapse simulations of a reinforced concrete building structure using the Applied Element Method, run as preliminary work for a research proposal. It was published on Zenodo on 14 July 2025 by José Adam, Nirvan Makoond, Giacomo Caredda, María Luz Gerbaudo, Andri Setiawan and Manuel Buitrago of the Universitat Politècnica de València. Three models share the same structural design: a bare frame benchmark (RC_00), a frame with a shear core (RC_SC) and a frame with infill walls at one end (RC_IW). Each was subjected to the same initial failure, the loss of two columns, to see how these features affect the spread of collapse. A workbook summarises the common design, the key results and a variable guide, and images show the partly collapsed structures from several views. Coverage: three simulated buildings. Access: one workbook and a set of PNG images on Zenodo. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; free. Caveats: preliminary feasibility results, not a validated study. Simulation uses: comparing robustness features in progressive collapse and cascading failure models of buildings. Related records: the collapse volume ratio fatality data and the NEES test datasets.
